catalog.status: accepted by the apps; not yet shipped

Slot.sum: A fixed box in a tool row for a part that depends on data arriving after the row is drawn: the call's phase and times, its record or completion, or the time.

box.d: code: the light code background, padded, holding exactly lines monospace lines, such as a command's last output lines

Slot.tree: While needs is given and absent, the content is not evaluated: the evaluated node carries waiting: true and no children, and the app draws the box in the loading look, or in the not-kept look once the loading window since the call's answer has passed. needs itself is never in the tree. Without needs, the content always shows.

geo.w: narrow: min(TW(8 zeros, body), W); short: min(TW(12 zeros, body), W); medium: min(TW(24 zeros, body), W); long: min(TW(40 zeros, body), W); fill: W
geo.note: The width counts the digit zero in the row's body style, the way a CSS ch unit does. In a Card row without wrap, Slots take their widths before the row's other fixed children, so a long code or label beside a Slot is cut to what the Slots leave, wherever the Slot sits in the row. The content is laid out in a column at the box's width and clipped to the box; text that doesn't fit ends its last visible line with an ellipsis. Content shorter than the box sits in it the way the row places a child: in a Card row, centred for align center and at the bottom for end, and at the top for start, stretch and anywhere outside a Card row. The box never grows, so a row's height never depends on what arrives later.

states.loading: a moving skeleton filling the box, still when the person asks for reduced motion
states.unavailable: the box still and muted: the record was pruned or never written
states.text: the content's text form, or nothing while loading

Elapsed.sum: How long a call ran, or has been running: a clock the app keeps ticking itself.

geo.note: start and end are Unix milliseconds. It shows (end, or now while end is absent) minus start as m:ss under an hour and h:mm:ss from an hour, capped at 9:59:59, in tabular digits aligned to the box's trailing edge. While end is absent the app ticks it once a second without evaluating the template again.

states.text: the same m:ss or h:mm:ss string

Agent.sum: An agent, drawn by the app from its own list of agents as a creature and a name.

geo.w: min(L(body) + k.gap.s + TW(16 zeros, body), W)
geo.note: The creature fills an L(body) square, then the name, cut with an ellipsis. While a creature loads, the square holds a plain disc. An id the app doesn't know shows the raw id from the box's leading edge, cut the same way, with no creature and no empty square; the box keeps its width.

states.text: the agent's name, or the id

Model.sum: A model, drawn in words from the app's own model names, such as Opus 5.5 · Anthropic.

geo.note: The model's name, cut with an ellipsis. An id the app doesn't know shows the raw id.

states.text: the model's name, or the id

OpenItem.sum: A link in a tool page to an ask, an artifact, a work item or the thread with another agent, which opens the app's own card or screen for it.

geo.note: The label is body text in the page's prose, measured by the app. It is a link when the id starts with ask_, art_ or wi_, or is peer: and an agent_ id, and the app can read the item on the computer that ran the call, and plain text otherwise, never a disabled control.

ToolHeader.sum: A tool row's first line: an icon, a title, a muted secondary text and the trailing status, its one Slot child. Each app draws it in its own type.

icon.d: each app maps the name to its own symbol

truncate.d: how the title is cut; middle for paths

geo.note: One line. Its width is laid out in this order: the Slot takes its own width, the icon an L(body) square and k.gap.s, the subtitle min(TW(subtitle, footnote), 0.4 * rest) in footnote, and the title the rest in headline, cut as truncate says. The subtitle is cut at its end within its share.

ToolText.sum: A block of text in a tool row or page: TextContent's text, size and maxLines, plus a monospace or serif font, a tone, and inline Markdown.

font.d: mono takes size small or default; serif takes default or large

tone.d: colours the whole block; absent or neutral draws the default text colour

markdown.d: inline Markdown only: code spans, emphasis, strong, strikethrough, and links drawn as their label; everything else stays literal

geo.h: markdown ? prose : T(text, style, W, maxLines)
geo.style: body: small footnote, default body, large title3; mono: small monoFootnote, default mono; serif: default serif, large serifTitle3
geo.note: With markdown the text is prose the app measures with the text system it draws with, as Styled is. A ToolText read outside a Slot may read only input, so even then its height can't change when a record lands.

Diff.sum: Changes to a file on a tool page: hunks of context, added, deleted and plain lines, with old and new line numbers when the hunk has starts.

hunks.record: {title?: string, oldStart?: number, newStart?: number, lines: list<{kind: context|add|delete|plain, text: string, marks?: list<{start: number, end: number}>}>}
hunks.d: marks are highlighted ranges in Unicode scalar values

geo.h: sum over hunks of (2*k.codePad + has(title)*(L(caption1) + k.gap.xs) + count(lines)*L(mono)) + (hunks - 1) * k.gap.m
geo.note: Lines never wrap; a long line scrolls sideways inside its hunk. With oldStart and newStart a line shows its numbers: context counts both, delete the old, add the new. At most 2,000 lines show in all; past that the last hunk ends with a line saying how many more. A line whose kind isn't known draws as plain, and an entry that isn't a line is skipped.

states.text: each line with its marker: two spaces, + or -

AppPage.sum: A tool page that is the app's own screen for an item: an ask, an artifact, a work item, or the thread with another agent (peer:<agent id>).

id.d: ask_, art_ or wi_ id, or peer: and an agent_ id for the thread between the chat's agent and that one

geo.note: It must be the page's only node. The app opens its own screen for the id; when the id is empty or the app can't open it on the computer that ran the call, it draws the default page with the call's input and output.
